title: Nutrition and Athletic Performance — Joint Position Statement (Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Dietitians of Canada, ACSM 2016)
content: Joint Position Statement, Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise 2016 — Energy intake must be adequate to support training load, growth, and health; low energy availability impairs performance and health (see also RED-S). Protein needs for athletes range roughly 1.2-2.0 g/kg/day depending on sport/training phase, higher than the general-population RDA. Carbohydrate needs scale with training volume/intensity (from ~3-5 g/kg/day for light training up to 8-12 g/kg/day for very high-volume endurance training) — a bodybuilding-style gym-goer typically needs far less than an endurance athlete.

title: Nutrition and Athletic Performance — Joint Position Statement (Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Dietitians of Canada, ACSM 2016)
content: ACSM/AND/DC 2016 — Fat should not be restricted below recommended levels (essential fatty acids, fat-soluble vitamin absorption, hormone production). Nutrient timing and food choices should be individualized to the athlete's sport, goals, body size, and preferences rather than a one-size-fits-all prescription; hydration status should be individually assessed (sweat rate, body-weight change), not prescribed as a single fixed daily water volume for everyone.
